name: Barossa Valley

climate: Shiraz, Cabernet Sauvignon and Grenache sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.

terms: Australia's Geographical Indications nest in three levels: zones, the regions inside them, and subregions inside those.
keyfacts: Barossa Valley Shiraz is full bodied, rich and robust, with notes such as blackberry, plum, black pepper and chocolate, and some Barossa Shiraz vines date back to the 1840s.
The Barossa zone covers both the warm Barossa Valley and the cooler Eden Valley, and wine labeled Barossa must contain at least 85% Barossa fruit.

notes: Barossa Shiraz, often from old vines, is big and full bodied, with rich chocolate and spice.
In this hot climate Shiraz has softer tannin, jammier fruit and notes of licorice, anise and earthy leather.
Barossa Grenache is jammy and intensely fruity.
Barossa Semillon is full bodied, golden and low in acidity, and the Chardonnay is often oaked, big and creamy.

blurb.text: A warm region about 35 miles northeast of Adelaide, in the Barossa zone of South Australia, settled in the 1840s by English and German settlers. Its warm, dry summers gave very ripe grapes and an early fortified wine industry. Shiraz is 65 percent of plantings, then Cabernet Sauvignon at 14 percent.
